title: An NP-hard language in P collapses P and NP
statement: Let $L$ be a language over the binary alphabet such that every language in $	extsf{NP}$ has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to $L$. If $L$ is decidable in polynomial time, then the class $	extsf{P}$ of polynomial-time decidable languages equals $	extsf{NP}$, where membership in $	extsf{NP}$ means having polynomial-length certificates verifiable in polynomial time.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is NP-hard under polynomial-time many-one reductions
replaced:
Let $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^{*}$ be an $\mathsf{NP}$-hard language, i.e.\ every
language in $\mathsf{NP}$ is polynomial-time Karp reducible to $L$. If
$L \in \mathsf{P}$, then $\mathsf{P} = \mathsf{NP}$ [AB09, Theorem~2.8.2].
